name: trooping fairies

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Trooping fairies are a class of fairy in folklore. Fairies came in two main kinds. Solitary fairies, such as the leprechaun, kept their own company and avoided others of their kind. The more common trooping fairies lived together in great palaces, where they danced and sang the day away. Some writers add a third kind, the domestic fairy, like the brownie. This fairy lived without other fairy kin but was friendly to people. Trooping fairies gave little trouble to humans who kept clear of them. Sometimes they rode forth on the Wild Hunt to seize babies and brides and take them to Fairyland.

okr.objective: Record the class of fairies called the trooping fairies.
